summary: The w11 fixes are in the renders. The teal belt now shows on the cushion (r7: 671 teal pixels, w11 had 0), the plaques sit at the cap ends, the cap is darker and the spine no longer crosses the centreline fins. From the aisle (q06, q08, q10) the room is clearly the same product: nested pairs, monuments, charcoal frames round the ash, monitors and consoles. Four things keep it below 8.5. (1) The O-bed comforter is still the weakest piece. In r6 and r9 it is a pale, glossy, crumpled periwinkle tongue with no quilting or jacquard. The real comforters (tpg_79, tpg_81, lalf_3) are opaque royal or indigo, about half the luma of the white pillow, with a clear check jacquard and soft broad folds. (2) The duvet is too light and too grey in both beds: about 0.66 of the white pillow's luma in the render against about 0.5 in the photos. (3) The ash renders pale cream: (181,177,171) against (125-162) in c_27312/15/16. Its grain contrast is about half the photos': high-pass/mean 0.045-0.072 against 0.12-0.22. An uncommitted re-cut of the ash tile from tpg_60 is in the working tree but is not in these renders. (4) Smaller items: the belt is cyan-teal where the photos show slate blue; the plaque glow quad paints a navy rectangle over the grey tile; and the spine still meets the cap at 80 % of its length (owner decision 12, still in place). Lighting: the shells read cool blue-slate in the cabin views (q10 shell (66,72,84)); this is not scored here.

issues.detail: O-bed comforter: glossy crumpled pastel tongue, with pinched ridges where it enters the footwell and no quilting or jacquard
issues.problem: r9 (340-420 x 200-290) shows tight parallel vertical ridges where the sheet narrows into the footwell wedge. The bounds() squeeze from 0.31 to fr while the DUVET_FOLDS and the head roll stay fixed, so the folds get compressed into pleats. The rest of the sheet is smooth, glossy and pastel, with no seams. tpg_79 and tpg_81 (both O beds, comforter tucked into the footwell) show an opaque comforter with ~0.3 m quilt boxes outlined by soft seams, a check jacquard over the whole surface, and 2-3 broad loose folds. In r6 the O sheet covers only the aisle half beside the seat, where tpg_81 shows it over ~85 % of the mattress width at the pillow end.
issues.evidence: r9 duvet (300-360 x 190-230) is (143,158,228), white pillow (245,244,243). tpg_81 duvet (700-1000 x 400-700) is (108,120,212), white pillow (242,226,203); after white balance by the pillow, the duvet is 0.45/0.53/1.04 of white against the render's 0.58/0.64/0.93.
issues.fix: 09c_room.js roomBed O branch: (a) Fade the folds out in the footwell instead of squeezing them: in fold(), multiply f by (1 - smooth(MON.zO - 0.25, MON.zO, z)) when hd > 0, and replace the footwell part of the sheet with a gentle 1.5 cm sag. (b) Widen the O sheet at the head: bounds xl lerp(-0.415, ...) -> -0.45, so the cloth covers the outer side up to the 3 cm pad margin seen in tpg_81. (c) Drop the irregular free-edge wobble amplitude 0.012/0.008 -> 0.006/0.004. (d) Pass foldK 0.5 (not 0.2) but with A capped at 0.02 so the quilt dip (0.020) stays dominant. (e) Material: see the duvet colour issue.

issues.detail: Duvet (both beds) too light, too grey and glossy; no jacquard
issues.problem: In both r9 and r10 the duvet renders pastel periwinkle at ~0.66 of the white pillow's luma. Real comforters are 0.47-0.53 of white (tpg_81, lalf_3) and more saturated, with a check jacquard like the pillow's. The satin specular on the pastel colour makes the sheet read translucent.
issues.evidence: r10 duvet (170-240 x 320-380) is (120,134,206) and its white (226,226,229). lalf_3 duvet (300-600 x 640-740) is (103,103,142) against a white pillow of (243,217,187), which white-balances to 0.42/0.47/0.76. tpg_81 white-balances to 0.45/0.53/1.04. The model is about 1.3x too light.
issues.fix: 09_seats.js (shared, one line): duvet { c: '#4d57aa', r: 0.7, l: LAYER.fabric } -> { c: '#3f4799', r: 0.8, l: LAYER.jPillow } (or LAYER.yagasuri if jPillow is not merged), with the UVs on duvetSheet scaled so the check repeats at ~2.5 cm (g.u.push(i/nu*1.2*12, j/nv*2.2*12) or whatever the pillow tile needs). Re-check r9 and r10 for duvet/white luma ~0.5.

issues.detail: Ash panels render pale cream with about half the photo's grain contrast
issues.problem: In the aisle views the privacy walls read as off-white linen, not the greige ash with visible straight streaks in the photos.
issues.fix: The uncommitted tpg_60 ash tile with PHOTO_GAIN[19] = 1.2 should roughly double the grain; verify after the rebuild (target q06 hp/mean >= 0.11). Then SEATMAT.ash '#dcd5c8' -> '#cdc4b6' (shared, one line), which brings the walls to ~0.85 of the current luma and a touch warmer. Keep the tables as they are if they are a separate material.

issues.detail: Belt reads cyan-teal; photos show slate blue-grey
issues.problem: The strap is also a flat, short bar floating on the cushion, not a strap that rises from the back/cushion seam.
issues.evidence: r7 belt (88,146,161) against r7 fabric (157,153,164): g-r +58. c_27315 belt (69,92,116): g-r +23, b-r +47. c_27313 (46,64,76). tpg_46 is a dark slate strap with a silver buckle.
issues.fix: 09c_room.js roomSeatCore: belt c '#30505a' -> '#38485a' (r 0.75). Add a second segment from the seat/back fillet: B.add(gBox(0.045, 0.004, 0.12), M4.mul(CU, M4.trs(0.20, 0.045, 0.27, -0.5 - 0.5)), belt), so it emerges from the crease.

issues.detail: Plaque glow quad paints a navy rectangle over the grey tile
issues.problem: The room tag quad (0.058 x 0.03) samples the atlas tag cell, whose background is '#3a3531', and tints it '#5f9dff' with emission 0.5. The whole quad therefore reads as a navy field, where c_27315 and tlfl_9211 show a grey tile with only the numerals lit.
issues.fix: 06_atlas.js line ~100: for room seats draw the tag cell background '#000000' (the glow layer then adds nothing outside the glyphs), or shrink the room quad to the glyph box (gQuad(0.040, 0.018)) and let the '#5c6066' plate show round it.

issues.detail: Upright blue pillow edge reads cream/white, not the grey flange
issues.problem: In r7 (330-450 x 230-450) the blue pillow carries a pale cream rim. tpg_46 and tpg_81 show the flange as a mid grey-taupe (tpg_81 flange visible at the pillow's lower edge).
issues.fix: Check SEATMAT.jPillowBack. If it is pale, set it near '#8f8a8c'. Also check that the flange loft (cushionSecs 0.458 x 0.358 x 0.008) is not picking up the white pillow's material through z-fighting.

questions: lalf_3 (2021) shows the crew-made bed with the comforter folded back across the full width and both pillows side by side at the head. tpg_79 and tpg_81 show it loose and tucked into the footwell. Which bed-mode look should the model show? (The current model follows tpg_81 loosely but covers less width.)
Night photos (tlfl_9211, 2024) show blue-lit plaque numerals; ANA's daytime c_27315 shows white. Keep blue (current), or switch to white for day moods?
